title: Slav Defence (2...c6)
intro: Black supports d5 with 2...c6. Play Nf3 and Nc3, stop ...b5 with 5.a4 after ...dxc4, and punish early ...Bf5 with Qb3.

lessons.title: The Slav main line
lessons.summary: Develop Nf3 and Nc3, then stop ...b5 with 5.a4.

steps.text: In the Slav Defence, Black backs up d5 with 2...c6, keeping the light-squared bishop free.
Develop your king's knight first to keep control of e5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.Nf3 to guard d4 and stop ...e5 counterattacks.
steps.ifRight: 3.Nf3 also avoids sharp gambits like 3.Nc3 dxc4 4.e4 b5.
Now Black must choose how to handle the tension on d5.

steps.text: Black accepts on c4 with 4...dxc4, planning to defend the pawn with ...b5.
Stop ...b5 right away so you can win c4 back easily.

feedback.e2e3: 5.e3 lets Black play 5...b5 and cling to the extra pawn.

steps.text: Black develops the bishop with 5...Bf5. Open the diagonal for your f1 bishop to recapture c4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.e3 (followed by Bxc4) to win your pawn back and prepare castling.
steps.ifRight: After 6...e6 7.Bxc4, White has a strong centre and easy play.

lessons.title: Punishing an early 3...Bf5
lessons.summary: Trade on d5 and hit b7 and d5 with Qb3.

steps.text: Sometimes Black rushes the bishop out with 3...Bf5 before playing ...Nf6 or ...e6.
Open the c-file and clear the way for your queen.
steps.ifRight: Once Black takes back, b7 is a target.

steps.text: Fork b7 and d5 with your queen.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Qb3 to attack both b7 and d5 at once.
steps.ifRight: Black is forced onto the defensive.

steps.text: Black defends b7 with 5...b6, weakening c6 and the light squares. Develop and put pressure on d5.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to attack d5 and control e4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nc3 (or 6.e4) to attack d5 and keep Black under heavy pressure.
steps.ifRight: White dominates the centre and dark squares.

feedback.e2e3: 6.e3 is too slow: 6.Nc3 or 6.e4 hits d5 while Black's queenside is loose.

steps.text: If Black plays 5...Qc7 to guard b7 and eye c1, defend c1 and hit d5.
steps.hint: Develop the b1 knight to c3, protecting c1 with your bishop and hitting d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nc3: now ...Qxc1+ is impossible and d5 is attacked.
steps.ifRight: White threatens Nxd5 and e4 with a clear advantage.

lessons.title: Quiet Slav ideas
lessons.summary: Play e3 and Bd3 against 4...e6 and 4...a6.

steps.text: Instead of 4...dxc4, Black often plays 4...e6 or 4...a6, keeping the tension.
Reinforce d4 calmly and avoid sharp sacrificial lines.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.e3 to build a solid structure.

steps.text: Put your light-squared bishop on its best attacking square.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Bd3 to support e4 and eye h7.
steps.ifRight: If Black takes on c4, Bxc4 develops with tempo.

steps.text: Black captures 6...dxc4. Win the pawn back immediately.
steps.hint: Take on c4 with your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Bxc4, gaining time and preparing O-O and e4.
steps.ifRight: White enjoys a strong centre and easy play.

steps.text: Against 4...a6, keep your centre solid and develop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.e3 (or 5.c5 or 5.a4) to keep a firm grip on the centre.
steps.ifRight: Simple and solid: White castles and fights for e4.
